text:
Alexis Lafreniere led the league in goals for a stretch of October, and his nine in 19 games are still a solid pace for the Rangers' first overall pick of 2020. The last ten games have been quieter, seven points and two goals, but the reason is mostly the ice around him: New York has scored 6.1 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on, while taking 56.5% of the five-on-five expected goals.

The flip side is his own shooting, 22% against a normal range of about 12.5 to 17%. That will drift down, so the two forces roughly cancel. Evolving-Hockey had him 29th among all forwards in wins above replacement last season, with real defensive value against tough competition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his offense lives on the rush (57% of his shots) and that he rarely carries the puck in himself.

Our projection lands him around 29 goals and 68 points. For a player once written off as a bust, that is a quietly excellent season.
headline: Lafreniere's goals came early, the quiet is luck
